_comment: Epic AI Chariot hardened Localhost seccomp profile (Wiz 'isolate and sandbox' gap #10). Opt-in via values.yaml seccomp.customProfile.enabled=true; RuntimeDefault stays the chart default. defaultAction ALLOW + an explicit deny list — NOT a full allow-list — because a hand-authored allow-list precise enough for the whole Node + napi runtime (ONNX/tokenizers/ed25519/aes-gcm/etc, CHARIOT-SPEC Phase 3) would be enormous and brittle across Node/glibc versions, and getting it even slightly wrong fails closed (breaks adapter/gateway startup). The deny list blocks the well-known container/sandbox-escape and system-tampering primitives while leaving the Node/napi runtime syscall surface untouched. This mirrors the deny list enforced by native/src/bin/seccomp_wrapper.rs (GAP #11, the npx/no-pod path) so both layers are maintained from one reviewed list. clone/clone3 are deliberately left off this list (unconditionally allowed) — this JSON profile format's per-argument matching was judged too hard to validate without a live kubelet/runc to test against, so no conditional CLONE_NEW*-flag denial is attempted here (unlike the BPF wrapper, which was tested end-to-end on the build host and does deny clone() when a CLONE_NEW* flag is set). Denying clone/clone3 outright would break Node's thread creation (libuv thread pool, worker_threads).

syscalls.comment: Namespace / mount / chroot primitives — container and mount-namespace escape vectors. unshare/setns cover the primary unprivileged namespace create-or-join calls.
Kernel/system tampering: module load/unload, kexec, reboot, swap, time/accounting.
Kernel keyring API — not used by the Node/napi runtime; a common credential-theft/persistence primitive when available.
bpf(2) and perf_event_open(2) — kernel introspection/tracing primitives with a history of privilege-escalation CVEs; not needed by the gateway.

Handle-based filesystem escape primitives (open_by_handle_at requires CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH to be useful, but denying it removes the syscall from the attack surface entirely) plus the paired lookup helper.
